title: Senior Character Animator
text:
**Join a leading AI lab's cutting-edge GenAI team to be at the core of the AI revolution, where your expertise fuels the development of the most advanced AI models.**

# 1\. Overview

A leading AI lab is building a performance transfer model: one that takes an actor's original performance and carries it faithfully into a new output, keeping the timing, the emotion and the small physical choices that make it feel real. We're looking for senior character animators who have spent their careers bringing acting to life on feature films, VFX and games, to help define what a well transferred performance looks like and judge where the model gets it right or wrong.

This is a part-time W-2 employment position with Cincinnatus LLC, with the opportunity to be placed at a leading AI Lab as part of their extended workforce.

# 2\. Key Responsibilities

- **Set the quality bar:** Define clear standards for when a performance has been carried over well, in body mechanics, facial nuance, timing and emotional intent, and point out where current evaluations fall short.
    
- **Critique model outputs:** Review generated performances shot by shot, the way you would in dailies, and write precise, actionable notes.
    
- **Build benchmarks:** Choose reference performances that range from easy to genuinely hard to capture, so the model is tested on what matters.
    
- **Shape the reviewer pool:** Help define the profile, rubric and calibration for the human reviewers who score outputs at scale.
    
- **Collaborate with other experts** to keep evaluations consistent and accurate.
    

# 3\. Core Qualifications

- 10+ years as a hands-on character animator focused on human and character acting, at Senior, Lead or Principal level.
    
- Animator credits on several feature films, VFX features or AAA game cinematics at recognized studios (e.g., Sony Pictures Imageworks, ILM, Animal Logic, Laika, Pixar, Disney, DreamWorks, Framestore, MPC, DNEG, Weta FX).
    
- A sharp eye for micro expressions, lip sync, weight and timing, and the small acting choices that make a performance feel authentic.
    
- Strongly preferred: facial animation experience, and recent work in real-time engines (Unreal or Unity), VR/XR, or performance capture pipelines.
    
- Hands-on use of generative image and video tools (e.g., Sora, Veo, Midjourney, Runway, Kling) to create your own samples for testing and comparison.
    
- Able to work on-site in Playa Vista (Los Angeles), CA or New York, NY for in-person working sessions once or twice a month.
    
- Strong written communication and the ability to turn visual detail into clear, precise language for evaluation templates.
    

**About Cincinnatus LLC:**
Cincinnatus LLC is an enterprise staffing company that partners with leading technology companies to source and employ highly skilled professionals for contingent and contract-based opportunities. Cincinnatus serves as the employer of record for these engagements, providing W-2 employment, payroll, benefits, and compliance, while placing employees directly within client teams to work on high-impact initiatives.

**Equal Employment Opportunity:**
Cincinnatus is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or any other legally protected characteristic.

text:
Role Title: Graphic and Editorial Design Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

###

Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $55 to $100 per hour

Location: Fully remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Professional experience designing for print, web or publications for a company, studio, publisher or client

Your tasks: Review designs and briefs, judge layout, readability and brief match, and explain your decisions in writing

You’ll review graphic and editorial design work and judge it: what works, what doesn’t, and why. This is a good fit if you work as a graphic designer, editorial designer, layout designer or art director and make decisions about how a page, a publication or a brand piece looks and reads.

### Scope of Work

- Look at designs (posters, covers, page layouts, brand pieces) and judge which one is stronger for a given brief and audience.

- Check hierarchy, spacing, type choices, color and how text and images work together.

- Flag problems that would show up in production (wrong format, low resolution, margins, print color).

- Check that a design fits the brief and the brand or publication style.

- Write a short explanation for each decision so a reviewer can follow your reasoning.

### What we’re looking for

- Professional work as a graphic designer, editorial designer, layout designer, publication designer, art director or brand designer.

- Daily use of professional tools such as InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop or Figma.

- Experience with real jobs: briefs, revisions, production files and delivery to a client or publisher.

- Comfort explaining why one design works and another doesn’t.

- Clear written English.

### How the selection process works

- Apply with your resume and a short profile.

- Complete the curation interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with exhibitions, collections and attribution. You don’t need to prepare, look at anything or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.

- Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.

- Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

title: Humanities Expert
text:
The research teams behind the best-known AI models come to Mercor for humanities judgment they can't generate on their own. Your standards and expertise become the rubric that frontier AI is graded against.

This is a standing listing for humanities scholars who want AI training and evaluation work, not a specific job opening. It stays open whether or not a matching project is running this week.

New projects start on short notice, so instead of posting and pulling a listing each time, we keep one open per field and draw from it when one begins.

**What the work looks like**

We match scholars in the network to projects like:

- Writing a question from your own field, with the sources, the context, and the interpretive problem, plus the reference answer a model's attempt gets graded against
- Grading model-written interpretation and argument: whether the sources say what the model claims, whether the reasoning holds, whether the historical or cultural context is right
- Flagging where a model produces fluent, confident prose that misreads the text, flattens a live scholarly debate, or invents a citation

Listings in this field on Mercor have posted at $45 to $60 an hour, set per project by scope and depth.

**What we're looking for**

- A graduate degree in a humanities field, or equivalent scholarly or professional experience
- Clear written communication, since most of the work involves explaining your reasoning
- Comfort with ambiguous tasks, and willingness to flag unclear instructions

**What this covers**

This pool spans the humanities, including:

- History; classics
- Philosophy; ethics and logic
- Literature
- Religious studies; cultural studies

Where you trained matters less than whether you can tell a strong reading from a merely plausible one, and say precisely where the weaker one fails.

**How it works**

Apply here with your resume and confirm where you work from, then take a short AI interview, about 20 minutes total.

We verify your background and add you to the humanities pool.

When a project needs your field, we invite matching people from the pool to that specific listing. It names the rate, the hours, and the client, and any hiring decision is made there.

**What to expect**

This listing does not accept or reject candidates, so you will not get a decision on it. We reach out when a project matches your background. Depending on what our clients are running, that can be within a week or several months.

Finishing the domain expert interview and joining every network you qualify for both improve your odds of being matched. You only need to sign up once to be eligible across all of them.

title: Finance Fellow - Human Frontier Collective (UK)
text:
PLEASE NOTE: This is a fully remote, 1099 independent contractor opportunity with an estimated duration of six months and the potential for extension. To be eligible, candidates must be authorized to work in the country they reside in.

### About the Program

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) Fellowship brings together top researchers and domain experts to collaborate on high-impact work that are shaping the future of AI. As an HFC Fellow, you’ll apply your academic and professional expertise to help design, evaluate, and interpret advanced generative AI systems—while gaining exposure to cutting-edge research and working alongside an interdisciplinary network of leading thinkers.

### What You'll Do

- Collaborative Work: Get invited to engage in high-impact projects with our partnered AI labs and platforms. Develop and evaluate complex financial scenarios to test and enhance AI accuracy in valuation, forecasting, and analysis; collaborate in interactive sessions to assess model outputs for market relevance and compliance; provide detailed feedback to improve AI capabilities; and contribute to specialized projects in financial modeling, risk assessment, and equity research.

- HFC Community: Beyond the work, you’ll become part of a supportive, interdisciplinary network of innovators and thought leaders committed to advancing frontier AI across domains.

- Contribute to Research Publications: Collaborate with Scale’s research team to co-author technical reports and research papers—boosting your academic visibility and professional recognition (e.g., SciPredict, PropensityBench, Professional Reasoning Benchmark).

### Who Should Apply

- Education: PhD, Master, BBA in Finance, Economics, or related degrees.

- Certifications: CFA or CPA strongly preferred.

- Professional Background: 5+ years in FP&A, Investment Banking, Portfolio Management, Financial Consulting, or equivalent research experience.

- Skills: Strong proficiency in financial modeling, valuation methodologies, forecasting, asset pricing, DCF analysis, market analysis, and risk assessment.

- Professional Mindset: Detail-oriented, innovative thinker with a passion for financial technology and a commitment to collaboration. Prior experience with AI is not required, but a plus.

### Why Join the HFC?

- Advance Finance AI Solutions: Apply your financial expertise to solve complex, real-world challenges where your judgment shapes advanced AI reasoning and decision-making.

- Professional Development: High-impact finance experts expand their influence through review projects, advisory roles, and research—while deepening their AI expertise, sharpening analytical and financial skills, and gaining hands-on experience with cutting-edge AI applications.

- Join a Top-Tier Network: Collaborate with a global network of academics and experts to advance responsible AI through impactful, flexible research and training. 80% of our members come from leading institutions.

- Flexible Schedule: Set your own schedule, with flexible 10–40 hour weeks that fit around your life and other commitments.

- Competitive Pay: Project pay rates vary across platforms and are depending on a number of factors, including but not limited to; projects, scope, skillset, and location.

### Application Process

- Apply: We review applications on a rolling basis.

- Complete a Challenge: Selected candidates will undertake a brief task designed to reflect HFC work and evaluate their domain expertise.

- Interview: Candidates will get to discuss their research experience, professional background, and alignment with our mission to advance human-centered AI.

- Join the Collective: Successful candidates will receive an invitation to join the Human Frontier Collective Fellowship.

PLEASE NOTE: Our policy requires a 90-day waiting period before reconsidering candidates for the same role. This allows us to ensure a fair and thorough evaluation of all applicants.

title: Chemical Defense Researcher
text:
## About the work

Mercor is assembling a panel of chemistry and chemical safety experts to red-team frontier AI models. The goal is to test whether a model can correctly judge the misuse potential of a technical request — answering legitimate questions fully while refusing genuinely dangerous ones.

You will:

- Write challenging single-turn prompts in your domain, labelled across three levels: benign, dual-use, and adversarial.
- Evaluate the responses that come back against a defined policy standard, and judge whether each was handled correctly.
- Write the reference answer — what a correct response looks like, and the technical reasoning for why.

This domain lives on the dual-use line more than most. The same toxicology that sets a countermeasure dose describes an exposure someone might intend; the same decontamination data that protects responders tells you what defeats it. A model that refuses a routine countermeasure or PPE question is failing as badly as one that answers a question it shouldn't. Drawing that line reliably is why we need practitioners rather than generalists.

## Background we're looking for

We're looking for people who have worked chemical threats from the defensive side in an institutional setting — countermeasures, protection, detection, verification. What matters most is being able to tell a routine professional question from one that's fishing for something else: the same agent properties that drive a treatment protocol drive a threat assessment. You will be writing prompts that sit exactly on that line, then judging whether the model held it.

Examples of relevant backgrounds (ideally with red-teaming experience):

- Chemical defence research at USAMRICD, DoD, CDC or an allied national institute
- Toxicology of chemical warfare agents and medical countermeasure development
- Decontamination, protection and detection research for chemical threats
- CWC-related work — verification, destruction, designated laboratory analysis
- Consequence assessment and medical management of chemical exposure

## What this role demands beyond technical depth

This is writing-intensive work. Every judgment you make needs a written rationale that a non-specialist can follow. Prior technical writing, published research, or expert witness experience is a strong signal; please include a sample or link. You will also be reading and writing about misuse scenarios in your field for sustained periods. We brief experts on this in advance, and you can pause or step away at any point without penalty.

## Before you apply

Your work here will not involve, and must not draw on, classified or export-controlled information, or anything covered by an NDA or prepublication review obligation. If you hold such obligations you may still be a good fit; tell us in your application and we will scope the work accordingly.

Role Title: Senior Specialty Inspection Expert, Crop, Auction and Rental

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Global-Remote

Job Type: Contractor (~10 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible-you choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired

micro1 is engaging Senior Specialty Inspection Experts, Crop, Auction and Rentals to support a customer's project in specialized inspection domains. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. This opportunity is designed for established professionals with deep inspection experience in crop condition and loss assessment, auction and pre-sale grading, and rental or lease return evaluations. You will analyze authentic inspection records, field or aerial photos, and documented imagery, producing assessments that reflect current industry best practices. Communication excellence, both written and verbal, is essential, as your insights will drive accurate training data for advanced technology platforms.

Scope of Work

- Review field and aerial imagery, as well as inspection records, to assess crop conditions and determine loss in line with insurance protocols.

- Evaluate vehicles and equipment for auction or pre-sale, assigning accurate condition grades using photographic evidence and inspection data.

- Analyze rental or lease return inspection records, identifying damage and detailing findings in clear, expert-level reports.

- Document and articulate the reasoning behind each grade or assessment, ensuring transparency and traceability of your conclusions.

- Collaborate remotely with project coordinators to clarify requirements and address project-specific needs.

- Provide high-quality, real-world input that will inform the development and refinement of AI models.

- Contribute expertise in one or more specialty areas; specify your area of focus during the engagement process.

Preferred Qualifications

- Minimum of 5 years’ professional experience in crop insurance adjusting, auction grading, or rental/lease return inspection.

- Demonstrated proficiency in interpreting field and aerial imagery for agricultural or industrial assessments.

- Thorough understanding of industry grading standards and loss assessment methodologies.

- Exceptional attention to detail in documentation and reporting.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce clear, well-supported justifications.

- Comfort with remote work environments and digital platforms for document review and communication.

- Experience across multiple specialty areas (crop, auction, rental) is a plus, but not required.
